note: AWS module is credential/client plumbing for aws/aws-sdk-php - it makes NO AWS API calls, so all cases are grounded in config entities and services only (no live AWS, no credentials needed). Code-grounded facts: AWS Profile = config entity type aws_profile (config aws.profile.<id>) with fields id,name,default,region,aws_access_key_id,aws_secret_access_key,aws_role_arn,aws_role_session_name,encryption_profile; service overrides in config aws.settings:services.<service_id>={profile,version}; service list comes from the SDK's Aws\manifest(); client built via aws.client_factory->getClient('s3') -> \Aws\S3\S3Client using Profile::getClientArgs(); credential order = role ARN (STS temp creds, cached) -> stored key/secret -> CredentialProvider::defaultProvider(); permission 'administer aws'. Medium cases install known config state (a profile's region; an S3 service override). Hard cases build real config state verified against live config entities: create a default profile with a region, and bind the S3 service to a profile. All fixtures namespaced aws_*; verify scripts only read Drupal config/entities, never call AWS.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal 'aws' (Amazon Web Services) module, how does custom code obtain a ready-configured AWS SDK client (e.g. an S3 client) for a given service?
evals.expected_output: Call the aws.client_factory service: \Drupal::service('aws.client_factory')->getClient('s3') returns an \Aws\S3\S3Client. The factory resolves a profile (explicit setProfile() -> per-service override -> default profile) and instantiates \Aws\<Namespace>\<Namespace>Client with the profile's getClientArgs() (credentials, region, version).

evals.prompt: In the Drupal aws module, how/where are AWS credentials and region stored, and what fields does a profile hold?
evals.expected_output: Credentials are stored as 'aws_profile' config entities (config aws.profile.<id>) with fields id, name, default, region, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key, aws_role_arn, aws_role_session_name and encryption_profile. Managed at /admin/config/services/aws (permission 'administer aws').

evals.prompt: In the Drupal aws module, how does a profile decide which AWS credentials to use when building a client (the resolution order)?
evals.expected_output: Profile::getClientArgs() resolves credentials in order: (1) if aws_role_arn is set, assume the role via STS and use the temporary credentials (cached in a key-value-expirable store); (2) else use the stored aws_access_key_id + aws_secret_access_key; (3) else fall back to the SDK's CredentialProvider::defaultProvider() (environment vars, EC2/ECS instance profile, etc.). Region and version are added too.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site an AWS profile has been configured with the 'aws' module. Inspect the live configuration and report the AWS region that profile is set to.
evals.expected_output: The aws_eval_profile profile has region us-west-2 (readable via `drush cget aws.profile.aws_eval_profile region`); it is also the default profile.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the aws module has a service override so the S3 service uses a specific AWS profile. Inspect the live configuration and give the machine id of the profile bound to the S3 service.
evals.expected_output: The S3 service override in aws.settings:services.s3 points at profile aws_svc_eval (readable via `drush cget aws.settings services` or \Drupal::service('aws')->getServiceConfig('s3')).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, using the aws module, create a new AWS profile for the eu-central-1 region and make it the default profile (used by services with no override). You do not need real credentials. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A new aws_profile config entity exists with region 'eu-central-1' and its default flag set (isDefault() TRUE) - created via the Add profile form at /admin/config/services/aws/add-profile or the aws_profile entity storage.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is an AWS profile with machine id aws_svc_profile. Using the aws module, configure a service override so the S3 service uses that profile. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: aws.settings:services.s3.profile is set to 'aws_svc_profile' - via the service-override form at /admin/config/services/aws/service/add (service s3) or \Drupal::service('aws')->setServiceConfig('s3', ['profile' => 'aws_svc_profile', 'version' => 'latest']).
